claims.text: Sliding a Cantor-type high-entropy alloy produces a refined near-surface microstructure.
The sliding-induced near-surface layer is partially amorphous.
The refined, partially amorphous near-surface layer disrupts the protective passive oxide film.
Disruption of the passive film accelerates localized chloride-induced corrosion.
Surface refinement increases the hardness of the sliding-affected layer.
Formation of the refined near-surface layer reduces wear.
The initial alloy has a coarse-grained microstructure.
The initial alloy has an intact, protective native passive oxide film.
Repeated sliding mechanically removes or damages the passive film.
Repassivation is too slow to restore the passive film between sliding events.
Fine grains and residual stress can weaken the passive layer and reduce the corrosion resistance of Cantor alloys.
The coupled tribo-corrosion response is governed by competition between wear reduction and corrosion acceleration.
Tribo-corrosion will produce a lower wear rate than isolated wear.
Tribo-corrosion will produce higher corrosion current density than static chloride immersion.
Tribo-corrosion will cause earlier pitting than static chloride immersion.
Total degradation under tribo-corrosion will exceed the sum of degradation from isolated wear and isolated corrosion.
The proposed mechanism requires chloride concentrations aggressive enough to attack the disrupted passive film.
The proposed mechanism requires sliding stresses high enough to cause substantial near-surface refinement.
The mechanism may fail in benign environments or when mechanical stress is too low to produce surface evolution.

contradictions.description: The prediction says tribo-corrosion has a lower wear rate than either isolated wear or corrosion, but the corrosion-only baseline is static immersion and therefore has no sliding wear rate against which a lower wear rate can meaningfully be predicted.
Load and sliding speed are said to be identical across tests, yet the corrosion-only control is static immersion and cannot share a nonzero sliding speed or applied sliding load.
